page.layout: One printed page, single column of running text, with a running head at the top; no margin notes; a catchword-free foot. Text runs from the head line down to the last line ending with "dici" (a catchword-like fragment "T" and "dici" sit at the foot).

main_text.p: quod præjudicia difpellat, passiones sedet, animum ad res applicet ut eas intelligat, quas cum non intelligimus, culpa penes nos est, nec ratio arcen-cenda est ex aliquo quod Scripturæ deficiat quæ in se sufficiens est ad arguendum & convincendum, teste Paulo Apostolo. Pariter si non convincantur Judæi singulis Prophetarum Vaticiniis, nec facilius illos convinci posse testimoniis in cumulum coacervatis, quia illa simul nihil probant, nisi antea seorsim singula expendantur, quæ si singula demonstrentur nihil habere roboris ad probandum, nec quicquam habebunt omnia simul coacervata.

Ad rem autem quod attinet, putabat omnia Prophetarum Vaticinia, sive simplicia, sive composita, sive in sensu litterali, sive in sensu mystico, apta esse ad convincendum, quia etiam in sensu mystico apta sunt ad assensum extorquendum, adeòque vim probandiinesse istis Evangelistarum formulis, ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τῶν Προφητῶν. Monebat autem τὸ πληρῆσν proprie quidem dici de mensurâ quæ impletur, cum antea esset vacua, sed etiam habere alias significationes, &c

page.notes: Greek line of the formula is printed in Greek; transcribed as best read. The letter "T" at the foot and the word "dici" may be a catchword or a fragment of the next line; the foot line reads "T dici" in print.
